verses.1: At that time, some people came forward and told him about the Galilaeans, and how Pilate’s blood was mixed with their sacrifices.
verses.2: And after answering, he said to them: “Do you think that the Galileans were sinners compared to all those people in Galilee? Do you really believe that they committed such sins?”
verses.3: No, I say, but if not all of you repent together, then you will be destroyed.
verses.4: And those eighteen people who were killed when the tower collapsed in Siloam… It seems that they were responsible for causing harm to all the people living in Jerusalem.
verses.5: No, I say, but if not all of you repent in the same way, then you will be destroyed.
verses.6: It was said that this was a metaphorical story. Someone planted some vines in his vineyard. He went to pick the fruit from those vines, but he couldn’t find any.
verses.7: He said to the vinegrower, “Look, three years have passed since I began to seek fruit from this vine. Yet I still haven’t found any fruit. I’ll cut down this vine. Why destroy not only the vine, but also the land itself?”
verses.8: But the one who answered said to him, “Lord, take her away from here, as well as this year. Until I can bury her and set up a tomb for her.”
verses.9: Even if he does create some benefit for the future—but if not, then you should cut it off.
verses.10: And he taught in one of the gatherings on Sundays.
verses.11: And I saw a woman who was weak and sickly for eighteen years. She couldn’t get up or stand up properly.
verses.12: When Jesus saw her, he called out to her and said, “Woman, you have been freed from your weakness.”
verses.13: And his hands were also cut off. But he was able to get back up again, and he honored the god.
verses.14: But when the leader of the crowd heard this, he was upset that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. He said to the crowd, “There are days in which we must not work. So go and be healed on those days, not on the Sabbath.”
verses.15: Then the Lord said to him, “Fools! On each of your Sabbaths do you not remove the ox or the lamb from its pen, and drink from it instead?”
verses.16: And this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had kept captive for ten and eight years, should not be freed from this bondage on the day of Sabbath.
verses.17: And while he was speaking these things, all those around him were terrified. Every single person in the crowd rushed towards those who were considered to be most respected by him.
verses.18: He said, “In what way is the kingdom of God similar to this? And in what way can I make it similar to it?”
verses.19: It is like a drop of blood from the eye. When a person takes it, it is placed in their own body. It then grows and becomes part of a tree. The drops of rain from the sky are trapped within its branches.
verses.20: And again he said, “In what way can I be equal to the kingdom of God?”
verses.21: It’s like a boil; when a woman takes it, she hides it in the sand until it fully boils.
verses.22: He also traveled from city to city and village, teaching there, and eventually making his way to Jerusalem.
verses.23: Someone said to him, “Lord, are there only a few who are going to be saved?” But he replied to them,
verses.24: Strive to enter through the narrow doorway. Many people, I say, will try to enter, but they won’t be able to do so.
verses.25: From where then the landlord will rise up and close the door. Then you should stand outside and try to open the door, saying, “Lord, please open for us.” When he replies, he will say, “I don’t know where you come from.”
verses.26: Then you should begin to say: “We will eat before you, and we will also learn from your actions.” And in our spaces, you will teach us.
verses.27: And I say to you: I don’t know where it is. Please leave me alone; all those who do evil deeds should be punished.
verses.28: There will be noise and turmoil among the people’s voices, when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God. But you will be sent out from there.
verses.29: And they will come from the east and from the west, from north and south. They will be gathered together in the kingdom of God.
verses.30: And it seems that there are those who will be first, and there are also those who will be last.
verses.31: In that time, some Pharisees came to him and said, “Go away from here! Herod wants to kill you.”
verses.32: And he said to them, “When you go there, say this to the demon. I will release demons and create nightmares for you today and tomorrow. On Wednesday, I will finish it.”
verses.33: In addition, I must go today and tomorrow, as well as on the day after that. For the prophet cannot be allowed to be destroyed outside of Jerusalem.
verses.34: Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You who destroyed the prophets and sent those who were sent to you away… How many times have I tried to teach your children how to protect themselves from the attacks of those who want to harm them, but you refused to do so.
verses.35: Behold, your home is coming to you. But I say to you, do not see me until I come. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
